html:
The Battle of Pliska, in July 811, was a disaster for the Byzantine Empire in which Khan Krum of Bulgaria destroyed the army of Emperor Nikephoros I in a mountain pass. It is also called the Battle of the Varbitsa Pass.

Nikephoros invaded the First Bulgarian Empire with a large army, refused Krum's offers of peace, and took and burned the Bulgar capital Pliska. While the Byzantines plundered, the Bulgarians blocked the passes through the Balkan Mountains with wooden walls. On 26 July they attacked the trapped camp at dawn. The emperor was killed with many of his officers, and his son Staurakios was badly wounded and died the next year.

Nikephoros was the first Roman emperor killed in battle since Valens at Adrianople in 378. The chronicles say Krum had his skull lined with silver and used it as a drinking cup. Krum went on to raid Thrace and reached the walls of Constantinople in 813.
